definitions.title: Definitions

definitions.howLocal: Local definitions have origin “local” and are never overwritten by the catalog. Built-in catalog entries are drafts: they are installed the first time you use them in an indexer.
definitions.howDraft: A draft state means the definition has not been verified against a real site. Open the detail page to see the YAML, validation problems and the indexers that use it.

applications.title: Applications
applications.subtitle: The *arr instances connected to indexarr. The API key stays encrypted in the vault and is never shown.
applications.levelDisabled: Disabled — the application stays configured but is never contacted and no indexer is added, updated or removed.
applications.levelAddRemove: Add/remove only — indexarr adds missing indexers and removes the ones it created that are no longer wanted, without updating existing ones.
applications.levelFull: Full sync — as above, but also updates the name, URL, key, categories, priority and options of existing indexers.
applications.manualNote: Indexers created by hand in the application are never modified or deleted.
applications.empty: No applications configured. Add Sonarr, Radarr or another client to sync the indexers.
applications.unavailable: The synchronization service is not configured: applications remain editable, but the Sync button reports the error.
applications.deleteConfirm: Delete this application? Indexers already present in the app are left untouched.
application.newSubtitle: Connect a Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Readarr, Whisparr, Mylar3 or LazyLibrarian instance.
application.editSubtitle: The API key is never shown: leave the field empty to keep the saved one.
application.name: Name
application.urlHelp: http:// or https:// address of the application, without the API path.
application.apiKeyHelp: The key is encrypted with the vault and never returned to the page.
application.deleteConfirm: Delete this application? Indexers already present in the app are left untouched.
import.title: Import
import.subtitle: Read the Prowlarr or Jackett configuration and build a migration plan for indexarr 2.
import.previewText1: The import only produces a plan: indexers, applications and proxies found in the source configuration. It does not create definitions, write to the database or modify Prowlarr or Jackett.
import.previewText2: Applying the plan will arrive together with native definition mapping. API keys, passwords and other secrets are not shown: the plan only says whether a value exists.
import.prowlarrURLHelp: Base URL of the instance, without /api/v1.
import.apiKeyHelp: Used only for this request and never shown in the plan.
import.jackettPathHelp: Directory containing ServerConfig.json and Indexers/, or the path to ServerConfig.json alone.
import.planPreview: Plan generated as a preview only: nothing has been saved.
import.noIndexers: No indexers found in the configuration.
import.noApplications: No applications found in the configuration.
import.noProxies: No proxies found in the configuration.

activity.subtitle: Scheduled or manual runs and process logs in one view.
runs.subtitle: Every scheduled or manual fetch, with its result.
logs.subtitle: In-memory process log, newest first. The same lines go to stdout and the systemd journal.
logs.levelHelp: Applied immediately and saved in the database; survives restarts.
logs.summary: Showing %d of %d captured (max %d); %d warnings/errors match the current filters.
logs.summaryLevel: Process level is %s; you can change it here without restarting. API keys, passwords and tokens are redacted.
logs.empty: No log lines match this filter. The buffer is empty after a restart or a clear.
logs.whereText: This page keeps the last %d records in memory; they disappear on restart or when you press Clear.
logs.whereJournal: With the systemd user service the full stream is also in the journal: journalctl --user -u indexarr -f. In Docker use docker logs -f indexarr.
logs.whereDebug: To see debug messages select Debug in Log level above; no restart is needed. log_level in indexarr.json is only the initial value.

settings.torznabEndpointLabel: Endpoint to give to Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr…
settings.regenerateConfirm: Generate a new API key? Every Torznab client will stop working until updated.
settings.additionalKeysHelp: Use one key per client (Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, a script). The primary key above cannot be revoked here; use the regenerate button.
settings.revokeConfirm: Revoke this API key? Its client will stop working.
settings.noKeys: No additional keys. Add one for each client that should have its own revocable key.
settings.defaultIntervalHelp: Used by sources that do not set their own. 3600 = hourly.
settings.fetchTimeoutHelp: Per request towards indexers and feeds.
settings.maxTorrentsHelp: Only items that expose a .torrent link but no magnet need a download.
settings.maxTorrentSizeHelp: Larger downloads are rejected instead of stored.
settings.fetchTorrentsHelp: When off, only magnets and metadata are stored.
settings.flaresolverrHelp: When an RSS feed or a direct indexer answers with a Cloudflare challenge, indexarr retries the same request through FlareSolverr. Leave empty to disable. Jackett and Prowlarr usually handle Cloudflare themselves, and a LAN address is never routed through FlareSolverr. The indexer URL, including its API key, is sent to FlareSolverr.
settings.flaresolverrTestHelpAfter: through the URL above; it does not save the settings and can take up to a minute.
settings.webhookHelp: Receives a JSON POST for new releases and failures. Leave empty to disable.
settings.telegramTokenHelp: Optional; it needs the chat ID too.
settings.telegramChatHelp: Set both Telegram fields, or neither.
settings.autoDisableHelp: 0 = never. A successful run resets the counter.
settings.apiRateLimit: API requests per key per minute
settings.apiRateLimitHelp: 0 = unlimited. Applied to the primary and every additional key; excess requests receive HTTP 429.
settings.liveSearch: Search indexers live on a cache miss
settings.liveSearchHelp: When the cache has no result, ask enabled Torznab sources (Jackett, Prowlarr, MirCrew, direct indexers) and store what they return. Off by default: it can make a client wait.
settings.liveSearchTimeoutHelp: Overall deadline for all queried sources. Sources that do not answer in time are ignored.
settings.downloadClientHelp: Adds a “Send to…” button on every release detail.
settings.backupsEnabledHelp: A consistent copy of the database, made with SQLite
settings.backupIntervalHelp: Checked every 30 seconds; the first backup runs soon after enabling.
settings.backupKeepHelp: Older automatic backups are removed. Pre-restore copies are kept.
settings.backupDirActions: List, download and restore from Maintenance.
settings.retentionHelp: 0 keeps everything. The cleanup runs every six hours and can be triggered from Maintenance.
settings.openWarning: The web interface is open to anyone who can reach the port. Set a user and password, or keep it behind a trusted network/reverse proxy.
